title: Travel and staying somewhere
description: Buy tickets, check buses and trains, and take a room in a hotel.

guide.title: Tickets, buses and trains
guide.text:
To buy a ticket, name the destination with the 'to' ending, then the number of tickets: maisoorige ondu tiket kodi, 'one ticket to Mysuru, please'; eradu tiket, 'two tickets'.

To check a bus or train: ee bas maisoorige hoguttaa? 'does this bus go to Mysuru?'. Buses and trains are neuter, so the verbs end in -utte: hogutte (goes), barutte (comes), horadutte (leaves), nillutte (stops).

Getting on and off: ಹತ್ತು (hattu) climb, get on - polite command ಹತ್ತಿ (hatti); ಇಳಿ (ili) get down, get off - polite command ಇಳಿಯಿರಿ (iliyiri). naanu illi iliyabeku, 'I need to get off here'.

ಸೀಟ್ (seet) seat; ಖಾಲಿ (khaali) empty, free; ಮುಂದಿನ ಸ್ಟಾಪ್ (mundina staap) the next stop; ಲಗೇಜ್ (lagej) luggage.

examples.english: Does this bus go to Mysuru?
I need to get off here.

guide.title: How long, how much per day
guide.text:
'How long?' is ಎಷ್ಟು ಹೊತ್ತು? (eshtu hottu?) - hottu means 'a stretch of time'. 'It takes two hours' is eradu gante aagutte, 'two hours happen'.

'Per' is the dative: ondu dinakke eshtu? 'how much for one day?'; talege nooru roopaayi, 'a hundred rupees a head'.

Lengths of stay take no ending: naanu mooru dina irteeni, 'I'll stay three days'; ondu vaara, 'for a week'.

'Until' is ತನಕ (tanaka) or ವರೆಗೆ (varege) after the time: shukravaara tanaka, 'until Friday'.

examples.english: How long does it take to the airport?

guide.title: At a hotel or guest house
guide.text:
ರೂಮ್ (room) is 'room'; the Kannada word ಕೋಣೆ (kone) is used for rooms of a house. room khaali ideyaa? asks whether a room is free. torisi, 'please show', lets you see it first.

Things to ask about use ide / ideyaa or barutte / baruttaa: bisi neeru baruttaa? 'does hot water come?'; vaifai ideyaa? 'is there wifi?'; e.si. ideyaa? 'is there air conditioning?'.

To ask permission use -abahudaa: illi idabahudaa? 'may I keep (it) here?'.

To find out what to see: illi nodoke enenide? 'what all is there to see here?'. enenu ('what all') is enu doubled; enenide is enenu + ide.

examples.english: Do you have a room free?
What is there to see here?

phrases.english: Does this bus go to Mysuru?
What time does the train arrive?
phrases.note: The Kannada word for train is railu (ರೈಲು).

phrases.english: I need to get off here.
phrases.note: The l of ili is the retroflex ಳ. Fast speech: ileebeku (ಇಳೀಬೇಕು).

phrases.english: How long does it take to the airport?
Do you have a room free?
May I leave my luggage here?
What is there to see here?
phrases.note: Both e of enen- are long.
